# Analysis Plan
<!-- Auto-generated by /new-analysis-plan. Edit freely, but preserve chunk IDs and status values. -->

## Project Summary

PhyloDistances.jl is a Julia package providing distance and similarity metrics between
pairs of phylogenetic trees. The target metric set is the union of the classical
branch-length-aware metrics (Robinson-Foulds and its weighted form, the
Kuhner-Felsenstein branch-score distance, path/cophenetic distance, quartet distance)
and the full metric inventory of the R package
[TreeDist](https://github.com/ms609/TreeDist) — the information-theoretic and
split-matching family (mutual clustering information, shared phylogenetic information,
clustering information distance, Nye similarity, Jaccard-Robinson-Foulds, matching split
distance and its information analogue, Kendall-Colijn, an NNI approximation, and maximum
agreement subtree measures).

Trees are ingested from Newick with NewickTree.jl and manipulated through the
AbstractTrees.jl interface, so the package is not tied to a single concrete node type.
The deliverable is the library API plus example and benchmark scripts; correctness is
established against analytically-known cases and against TreeDist reference values.

**Near-term priority**: Robinson-Foulds and quartet distance must be usable and validated
as early as possible — they are needed for immediate work. CHUNK-001 through CHUNK-008
form that critical path; everything after CHUNK-008 is expansion.

## Language & Environment

- **Language**: Julia 1.12 (minimum supported version; no LTS back-support)
- **Key libraries**: NewickTree.jl (Newick parsing), AbstractTrees.jl (traversal
  interface). Anticipated: a bitset/`BitVector`-based split representation,
  Combinatorics.jl for quartet enumeration. Test-only: Test, Random, StableRNGs (or
  seeded `Random.Xoshiro`) for reproducible synthetic trees. Optional weak dependency:
  Makie for visualization extensions. **No assignment-solver dependency** — the optimal
  assignment routine is vendored (see CHUNK-010).
- **Environment file**: `Project.toml` (to be generated in CHUNK-001)
- **Project maturity target**: `package`
- **Package name(s)**: PhyloDistances.jl
- **Extending existing package(s)**: no

## Working stance

Paper-quality reproducibility. Every chunk must be publication-defensible: full
docstrings, edge-case tests, and traceability from result back to code. Prefer getting
each chunk right the first time over leaving TODOs. When an adjacent finding or
improvement surfaces mid-chunk, record it in Open Questions rather than acting on it.

Corollary for this project: each metric's docstring must cite the primary reference
(author, year, journal) that defines it, and state precisely which variant is
implemented — several of these metrics have multiple published formulations that
disagree in normalization or in the treatment of trivial splits.

## Design decisions (settled)

These are user decisions, not open questions. They bind every chunk.

1. **Rooting: unrooted by default.** Trees are treated as unrooted unless a metric
   requires otherwise. Passing a rooted tree to an unrooted metric, or an unrooted tree
   to a rooted metric, emits a **warning** and proceeds under an explicit, documented
   conversion (drop the root split / apply the documented rooting rule). The warning must
   name the tree, the metric, and the conversion applied. Where no defensible automatic
   conversion exists, throw instead of warning — a warning is only appropriate when the
   package can state exactly what it did.

2. **Convention: TreeDist first, primary source behind a flag.** Every metric's default
   behavior reproduces TreeDist's, so CHUNK-021 can cross-validate the whole suite against
   it. Where a metric's primary source defines a different normalization or variant, that
   form is available through a `convention` keyword (`:treedist` default,
   `:primary` opt-in). The API must carry this flag from CHUNK-002 onward; retrofitting it
   later would touch every metric.

3. **Assignment solver: vendored.** The optimal-assignment routine underlying the
   generalized-RF family is implemented inside PhyloDistances rather than taken from
   Hungarian.jl, which is unmaintained relative to the pace of Julia's evolution. It is
   internal, not exported, and covered by its own tests against brute-force enumeration.

## Target Outputs

**Predictable (contract-style) outputs:**

1. **A reference-value regression table.** A committed fixture (`test/fixtures/`) of small
   named tree pairs with the expected value of every implemented metric, sourced from
   TreeDist and from hand-computable cases. This is the project's primary correctness
   artifact and its main claim to reproducibility. It must be small, plain-text, and
   documented as to provenance. Seeded early for RF and quartet distance (CHUNK-008),
   extended to the full metric set in CHUNK-021.

2. **A benchmark table.** `scripts/benchmark_metrics.jl` reporting runtime and allocation
   for each metric across tree sizes (n = 10, 50, 200, 1000 tips), so scaling behavior is
   visible and regressions are detectable.

3. **A metric-comparison figure.** `scripts/compare_metrics.jl` producing a
   pairwise-scatter/correlation view of all metrics evaluated over a common set of
   perturbed trees. This is the single most informative alignment artifact: metrics that
   are implemented correctly occupy known relative positions, and an implementation bug
   usually shows up as an outlier metric in this view.

**Composable visualization primitives** (exploratory; build these as reusable functions,
not one-off scripts — likely in a Makie package extension so Makie stays a weak
dependency):

- `plot_distance_matrix(D; labels)` — heatmap of an all-pairs distance matrix.
- `plot_treespace(D; method=:pcoa)` — 2-D embedding of a tree set under a chosen metric,
  for visually inspecting whether a metric separates known tree classes.
- `plot_metric_scatter(D1, D2)` — one metric against another over the same tree pairs.
- `plot_splits(tree)` — render a tree's split set as a taxon × split incidence matrix;
  the workhorse diagnostic for debugging split extraction and split matching.

**Ephemeral (do not commit):** per-chunk debugging views — printing a single split
matching, inspecting one quartet enumeration, comparing two candidate normalizations.
Produce these live in the MCP Julia session and let them go when it exits.

### CHUNK-001: scaffold-package
- **Description**: Generate the package with PkgTemplates.jl (`Tests`, `GitHubActions`,
  `Codecov`, `License`, `ProjectFile` with Julia 1.12 floor). Resulting structure:
  `Project.toml`, `src/PhyloDistances.jl`, `test/runtests.jl`, `scripts/`,
  `test/fixtures/`. Add NewickTree and AbstractTrees as deps with `[compat]` bounds
  chosen to be satisfiable on Julia 1.12, then `Pkg.resolve()`. Preserve the existing
  `LICENSE`, `README.md`, and `.gitignore` — do not let the generator clobber them.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Verification strategy**: `using PhyloDistances` loads cleanly; `Pkg.test()` passes on
  an empty test suite.
- **Notes**: PkgTemplates refuses to generate into an existing directory, so the skeleton
  was generated in a scratch directory and the wanted files copied in; `LICENSE` (MIT),
  `README.md`, and `.gitignore` are the originals, untouched. License/Readme/CompatHelper/
  TagBot/Dependabot plugins disabled. UUID `e638b194-4f2e-495a-b9ca-cc8e07bda67d`.

  Tests use a **separate test environment** (`test/Project.toml`), not `[extras]`/
  `[targets]` — test-only dependencies go there.

  Compat: `AbstractTrees = "0.4.5"`, `NewickTree = "0.4.0"` (both are the newest registered
  versions), `julia = "1.12"`. CI matrix is `1.12`, `1`, `pre` on ubuntu/x64.

  `scripts/` and `test/fixtures/` exist with `.gitkeep` placeholders; delete each when it
  gains real content.

### CHUNK-002: design-distance-api
- **Description**: Establish the public API shape before any metric is implemented, and
  record it in a docstring on the module plus a short section in `README.md`. Decide: (a)
  whether the entry point is trait/singleton dispatch (`treedistance(RobinsonFoulds(),
  t1, t2)`), per-metric functions (`robinsonfoulds(t1, t2)`), or both; (b) how
  normalization is requested; (c) whether similarities and distances are separate names or
  one family with a conversion. Two things are fixed by the settled design decisions and
  must be built in here, not retrofitted:
  - a `convention` keyword (`:treedist` default, `:primary` opt-in) threaded through the
    dispatch so per-metric variants land cleanly in CHUNK-022;
  - a rooting trait on each metric type (`isrooted(::Metric)`) that the shared
    precondition check in CHUNK-003 consults to decide whether to warn and convert.

  Also ship a **naive generic all-pairs fallback** (loop over pairs, call the pairwise
  method) so a distance matrix over a tree collection works from day one. CHUNK-024
  replaces it with the preprocessing-hoisted version; the API must not change when it
  does.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-001
- **Verification strategy**: A dummy test metric defined in the test suite dispatches
  correctly through every documented entry point, including the all-pairs path, both
  `convention` values, and both rooting traits.
- **Notes**: This chunk sets the cost of every later chunk. Because ~15 metrics must fit
  the same surface, favor a trait/singleton design that makes adding a metric a matter of
  defining one type and one method.

### CHUNK-003: tree-ingest-and-taxa
- **Description**: Newick ingest via NewickTree.jl, plus canonical taxon indexing: given a
  tree, produce the sorted leaf-label vector and a label→index map; given two trees,
  validate that they span the same taxon set and throw an informative error naming the
  differing labels if not. Implement the rooting policy from the settled design decisions:
  a predicate detecting whether a parsed tree is rooted, and a shared precondition helper
  that compares the tree's rooting against the metric's `isrooted` trait, warns with a
  message naming tree, metric, and conversion, and applies that conversion — or throws
  when no defensible conversion exists. All traversal goes through AbstractTrees.jl so the
  code works for any conforming node type, not only `NewickTree.Node`.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-002
- **Verification strategy**: Synthetic Newick strings constructed in the test itself (no
  external files); assert the taxon vector, the index map, that mismatched taxon sets
  throw with a message naming the offending labels (`@test_throws "..."`), and that the
  rooting mismatch path emits the expected warning (`@test_logs`) and returns the
  converted tree.
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-004: split-extraction
- **Description**: Extract the bipartition (split) set of a tree as bitsets over the
  canonical taxon indexing from CHUNK-003, with each split's supporting branch length
  attached. Provide canonical orientation (e.g. the side not containing taxon 1), a
  `Splits` container type with set operations, and a documented policy on trivial splits
  (pendant edges) and on the root split for rooted trees. This is the shared substrate for
  the entire RF and generalized-RF family.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-003
- **Outputs**: `Splits` type; `splits(tree)`.
- **Verification strategy**: Hand-computed split sets for small trees written as literals
  in the test; invariant assertions — a binary tree on n tips has n−3 non-trivial splits
  (unrooted) / n−2 (rooted); splits are invariant to leaf-label permutation composed with
  reindexing; canonical orientation is idempotent.
- **Notes**: Build the `plot_splits` primitive from Target Outputs here if split debugging
  demands it — the incidence view is the fastest way to spot orientation and
  trivial-split bugs. CHUNK-025 consolidates it with the other plots.

### CHUNK-005: random-tree-generation
- **Description**: Seeded generators for test fixtures: uniform random topology on n tips,
  random branch lengths, and controlled perturbation (apply k random NNI moves to a tree,
  returning the perturbed tree). The perturbation generator gives approximate ground truth
  — distance should increase monotonically in expectation with k — which is the main tool
  for validating metrics that have no closed form.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-003
- **Verification strategy**: Generated trees are valid (correct tip count, every internal
  node has ≥2 children, no repeated labels); output is reproducible under a fixed seed.
- **Notes**: Test-support code, but it belongs in `src/` (documented and tested) rather
  than `test/` so the benchmark and comparison scripts can use it too.

### CHUNK-006: robinson-foulds
- **Description**: Robinson-Foulds distance (symmetric difference of non-trivial split
  sets) and weighted RF (sum of branch-length differences over the symmetric difference).
  Include the normalized variants and document the normalizer used. Default convention is
  TreeDist's.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-004
- **Verification strategy**: Identical trees → 0; a tree against its own NNI neighbor → 2;
  maximally different binary trees on n tips → 2(n−3) unrooted; agreement with
  hand-computed cases.
- **Notes**: First metric on the critical path.

### CHUNK-007: quartet-distance-exact
- **Description**: Quartet distance — the number of four-taxon subsets whose induced
  topology differs between the trees — by direct O(n⁴) enumeration over taxon quadruples.
  This is deliberately the naive algorithm: it is the correctness reference for CHUNK-018's
  fast version, and it is fast enough for immediate use at modest tip counts. The docstring
  must state the complexity plainly so the performance ceiling is not a surprise.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-004
- **Verification strategy**: Identical trees → 0; a fully resolved tree against a star tree
  gives the known total quartet count C(n,4); hand-computed cases on 5 and 6 tips;
  symmetry in the arguments.
- **Notes**: Second metric on the critical path. Resist optimizing here — CHUNK-018 exists
  for that, and this implementation's value is that it is obviously correct.

### CHUNK-008: validate-rf-and-quartet
- **Description**: Early validation milestone. Seed the reference-value fixture described
  in Target Outputs with the tree pairs needed for RF and quartet distance (identical, one
  NNI apart, maximally different, a rooted input to exercise the warning path, a case with
  a polytomy, a case with zero-length branches), each with expected values and a
  provenance line. Add the test set that checks both metrics against it, and confirm the
  naive all-pairs API from CHUNK-002 produces a sensible distance matrix over a small tree
  collection.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-006, CHUNK-007
- **Verification strategy**: The fixture is plain text with no absolute paths, and the
  tests pass on a clean machine with no R installation and no network access. Expected
  values come from analytically-known results and hand computation; a TreeDist cross-check
  is a bonus, not a prerequisite — RF and quartet distance both have unambiguous ground
  truth that does not require R to establish.
- **Notes**: **This is the "usable today" checkpoint.** After this chunk, RF and quartet
  distance are validated and callable on real trees. Everything below is expansion, and
  can be reordered freely to suit what is needed next.

### CHUNK-009: branch-score-distance
- **Description**: Kuhner-Felsenstein branch-score distance: the Euclidean distance
  between the two trees' branch-length vectors indexed by split, with absent splits
  contributing length zero. Include the L1 variant if the chosen reference defines one,
  and document which norm the unqualified name refers to.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-004
- **Verification strategy**: Identical topology with identical lengths → 0; identical
  topology with lengths differing by δ on one edge → δ; metric axioms (symmetry, triangle
  inequality) spot-checked on random triples.
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-010: split-matching-framework
- **Description**: The generalized-RF engine, with a **vendored** optimal-assignment
  solver per the settled design decisions. Given the split sets of two trees and a
  pairwise split-similarity function, find the maximum-weight matching between them and
  reduce to a score. Nye similarity, JRF, matching split, and all four
  information-theoretic metrics are instances of this framework differing only in the
  pairwise scoring function. Expose the framework as a documented public entry point so
  users can supply their own scoring function; keep the solver internal.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-004
- **Verification strategy**: The vendored solver is checked against brute-force
  permutation search over all matchings for cost matrices small enough to enumerate
  exhaustively (≤8×8), including rectangular and tied-cost cases. The framework itself is
  checked for symmetry in its two arguments.
- **Notes**: Getting this chunk right collapses CHUNK-011 through CHUNK-015 into scoring
  functions plus tests. Since the solver is vendored, its test set is part of the
  package's correctness surface — treat it as a first-class component, not a helper.

### CHUNK-011: nye-similarity-and-jrf
- **Description**: Nye et al. similarity — each split pair scored by the size of the
  largest split consistent with both, normalized by the Jaccard index — and the
  Jaccard-Robinson-Foulds extension with its `k` exponent and its conflict-treatment
  parameter. Implemented as scoring functions plugged into CHUNK-010.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-010
- **Verification strategy**: Hand-computed scores for individual split pairs; identical
  trees → maximal similarity; the documented JRF parameter values that reduce it to RF
  actually do so.
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-012: matching-split-distance
- **Description**: Matching split distance — split pairs scored by the number of leaves
  that must move to make them identical, minimized over the matching. A scoring function
  for CHUNK-010.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-010
- **Verification strategy**: Hand-computed cases; identical trees → 0.
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-013: split-information-primitives
- **Description**: The information-theoretic quantities that the TreeDist information
  metrics are built from: the phylogenetic information content of a split (the log of the
  proportion of trees containing it), the clustering entropy of a split treated as a
  two-class partition, and the mutual information / joint entropy of a pair of splits.
  Includes the double-factorial tree-count machinery and its overflow-safe log form.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-004
- **Verification strategy**: Analytical checks — the number of unrooted binary trees on n
  tips matches the known double-factorial sequence; entropy of a balanced split equals
  1 bit; mutual information of a split with itself equals its entropy; all quantities
  non-negative and finite for n up to at least 1000 (overflow guard).
- **Notes**: Document the log base used (bits vs nats) once, here, and be consistent
  across every downstream metric — this is a common source of published-value mismatches.

### CHUNK-014: clustering-information-metrics
- **Description**: Mutual clustering information (MCI) and the clustering information
  distance (CID), as split-matching problems scored by the mutual information of the two
  splits' induced partitions, plus the normalizations TreeDist documents.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-010, CHUNK-013
- **Verification strategy**: Identical trees → maximal MCI / zero CID; CID satisfies the
  metric axioms on random triples.
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-015: phylogenetic-information-metrics
- **Description**: Shared phylogenetic information (SPI) — the conservative variant that
  assigns zero to incompatible split pairs — and the matching split information distance
  (MSID). Both are scoring functions over CHUNK-010 using CHUNK-013's quantities.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-010, CHUNK-013
- **Verification strategy**: Incompatible split pairs score exactly zero under SPI (assert
  directly on constructed pairs); identical trees maximize SPI.
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-016: path-distance-primitives
- **Description**: Pairwise leaf-to-leaf path representations: the patristic (summed
  branch length) distance matrix and the topological (edge count) path matrix, both
  indexed by the canonical taxon ordering. Computed by an LCA-based traversal rather than
  n² independent root-walks.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-003
- **Verification strategy**: Hand-computed matrices for a small tree; symmetry and zero
  diagonal; the four-point condition holds for any tree metric; ultrametric trees give
  equal root-to-tip patristic distances.
- **Notes**: Also serves the `plot_distance_matrix` primitive from Target Outputs.

### CHUNK-017: path-and-kendall-colijn
- **Description**: The path-length (cophenetic) distance — Euclidean distance between the
  two trees' path matrices — and the Kendall-Colijn distance, which interpolates between
  a topological and a branch-length vector via the λ parameter.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-016
- **Verification strategy**: Identical trees → 0; Kendall-Colijn at λ=0 and λ=1 reduce to
  the documented purely-topological and purely-length forms respectively.
- **Notes**: Kendall-Colijn is the package's main rooted metric, so it is the primary
  exercise of the rooting-mismatch warning path from CHUNK-003. Confirm that an unrooted
  input warns, names the rooting rule applied, and produces the documented result.

### CHUNK-018: quartet-distance-fast
- **Description**: Replace CHUNK-007's O(n⁴) enumeration with a subquadratic-in-quartets
  counting scheme, keeping the naive version available (internal, or behind an `algorithm`
  keyword) as the correctness oracle. Document the complexity achieved.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-007
- **Verification strategy**: The fast implementation agrees exactly with brute-force
  enumeration on random trees up to n=12, and on the CHUNK-008 fixture.
- **Notes**: Optional — skip if CHUNK-007's performance proves adequate for the tip counts
  actually in use. Decide from the CHUNK-026 benchmark rather than in advance.

### CHUNK-019: nni-distance-approximation
- **Description**: Approximate nearest-neighbour-interchange distance following the Li et
  al. bounds that TreeDist implements — lower and upper bounds plus the approximation,
  returned in a form that makes clear it is not exact.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-004
- **Verification strategy**: For trees generated k NNI moves apart (CHUNK-005), the
  returned lower bound never exceeds k and the upper bound never falls below the true
  distance for small cases where exhaustive search is feasible.
- **Notes**: The docstring must state prominently that this is an approximation and give
  its guarantees; silently returning an approximation under a name that reads exact is the
  main correctness hazard here.

### CHUNK-020: maximum-agreement-subtree
- **Description**: Maximum agreement subtree (MAST) size — the largest leaf set on which
  the two trees induce identical topologies — and its information-content variant using
  CHUNK-013's quantities.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-004, CHUNK-013
- **Verification strategy**: Identical trees → all n leaves; brute-force agreement over
  all leaf subsets for n ≤ 10; monotonicity — MAST size is non-increasing as NNI
  perturbations accumulate.
- **Notes**:

- **Description**: Extend the CHUNK-008 fixture to every implemented metric, with values

- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-009, CHUNK-011, CHUNK-012, CHUNK-014, CHUNK-015, CHUNK-017,

### CHUNK-022: primary-source-conventions
- **Description**: Implement the `convention = :primary` branch for every metric whose
  primary source differs from TreeDist's formulation. For each, the docstring states both
  forms, cites the primary reference, and explains the difference (normalizer, trivial-
  split treatment, log base, rooting assumption). Metrics where the two agree should say
  so explicitly rather than leaving the reader to infer it.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-021
- **Verification strategy**: For each metric, a test asserting the two conventions differ
  exactly where documented and agree exactly where documented; hand-computed expected
  values under the primary convention for at least one tree pair per metric.
- **Notes**: The audit of which metrics actually diverge is part of this chunk — record
  the finding in Working knowledge, since it is a durable fact about the literature rather
  than a code detail.

### CHUNK-023: polytomy-and-edge-case-handling
- **Description**: Audit every metric for behavior on non-binary trees, trees with
  zero-length or missing branch lengths, trees with two tips, and trees with a single
  internal node. Decide per metric whether the case is supported, errors informatively, or
  is documented as undefined — and make the code do exactly what the docstring says.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-021
- **Verification strategy**: A dedicated test set exercising each edge case against each
  metric, asserting either a specific value or a specific error message.
- **Notes**: Consistent with fail-fast: prefer an informative error over a plausible-
  looking number computed from an assumption the caller did not make. The rooting-mismatch
  warning is the deliberate exception, and only because it names the conversion it applied.

### CHUNK-024: all-pairs-optimization
- **Description**: Replace CHUNK-002's naive all-pairs fallback with a version that
  exploits symmetry and hoists per-tree preprocessing (taxon indexing, split extraction,
  path matrices) out of the inner loop so it runs once per tree rather than once per pair.
  The public API must not change.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-021
- **Verification strategy**: The matrix agrees entrywise with repeated pairwise calls; the
  diagonal is zero (or maximal, for similarities); preprocessing allocations scale as O(n)
  in the number of trees rather than O(n²).
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-027: docstrings-and-readme
- **Description**: Final documentation pass. Every exported symbol has a docstring giving

  `convention` value, the normalization, the rooted/unrooted requirement, and its
  complexity. `README.md` gains a metric table (name, function, reference, rooted?, uses
  branch lengths?, conventions available) and a short usage example. Verify no exported
  symbol is undocumented.
- **Status**: `not-started`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-026
- **Verification strategy**: A test asserting every exported symbol has an entry in
  `Base.Docs.meta`; doctests in the README example pass.
- **Notes**: Consider running `/freshen-docstrings` and `/freshen-package` at this point
  rather than doing the audit by hand.

## Open Questions

- **Rooting conversion rules.** The policy is settled (warn and convert), but the specific
  conversion for each direction is not. Unrooted → rooted needs a documented rooting rule
  (midpoint? outgroup-required?); rooted → unrooted needs a documented root-split policy.
  Resolve in CHUNK-003 and record in Working knowledge — the choice is visible in every
  warning message the package emits.
- **Quartet distance algorithm.** Whether CHUNK-018's subquadratic version is worth
  implementing. Deferred until the CHUNK-026 benchmark shows what CHUNK-007 actually costs
  at the tip counts in use.
- **Package granularity.** Split extraction (CHUNK-004), the vendored assignment solver
  and matching framework (CHUNK-010), and random tree generation (CHUNK-005) are all
  generically useful beyond tree distances. The assignment solver in particular is a
  candidate for its own package given that vendoring it was motivated by the lack of a
  maintained one. Revisit after CHUNK-010.
- **TBR distance.** TreeDist defers Tree Bisection and Reconnection distance to a separate
  package (TBRDist). Not planned here; note if it should be added later.
- **Generic indexing contract.** Path matrices and split bitsets are array-returning
  APIs. Decide whether to honor the `AbstractArray` contract for offset/view inputs or to
  declare `Base.require_one_based_indexing`. Recommendation: declare the 1-based
  assumption explicitly — the canonical taxon indexing makes it natural — rather than
  leaving it implicit.
